A general entity test will use a valid public ID mapped to the classpath DTD, where the system ID is ignored and internal subset entities may still resolve.

system-ok.xml references an external DTD at file:///output/csfix/ok. This is strong evidence of a trust boundary violation.

The external DTD was loaded and applied for validation despite the default-disabled flag. This is a behavior change. The parser reads a local file URI when untrusted configuration supplies it. It is not RCE. It is not SSRF because no network URL was tested. The code explicitly labels this a security problem. Severity is being weighed.

Ordinary parser crashes and trusted-configuration behavior are not automatically P0. The impact is a successful audit from a local file read, not secret exfiltration. A well-formed DTD could also pull file contents via external entities. A new crash candidate was found: entity.xml triggers an NPE in XMLDTDProcessor.endDTD because fTableOfNOTATIONAttributeNames is null.

The entity.xml NPE is an ordinary parser crash. It requires a malicious configuration and is not P0. The external DTD loading is the only real candidate.

The NPE is a second concrete failure. A crafted configuration with an external entity causes an unhandled NullPointerException instead of a clean SAX error. This aborts the CLI with exit code 1 rather than throwing a CheckstyleException. It is not a security leak. Severity is provisional P4 or P3. The external DTD loading remains the first candidate. The NPE is the second.

The entity.xml NPE is being reconsidered as ordinary JDK noise rather than a security bypass. It is a messy edge case inside Xerces when entity features are disabled but a SYSTEM entity is declared. It will be noted as an observed crash with provisional P4 severity, not as a security candidate. The buffer race remains the second candidate.

The buffer race is dropped. Only two observed failures will be reported. The NPE is confirmed at XMLDTDProcessor.endDTD line 1301. It is triggered from endEntity.
